title: Predicting clinical events characterizing the progression of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis via machine learning approaches using routine visits data: a feasibility study.
summary: Logistic-regression and multilayer-perceptron models learned from routine ALS registry visits to predict death, gastrostomy and non-invasive ventilation, with SHAP analysis of the predictors. The feasibility study reports independent-test AUROC and AUPRC above 0.8 for several progression outcomes. The study does not establish external generalization, causal effects or sustained operational impact.
